source.title: Chiefs and Families of Note in the Punjab
source.limitations: Retrospective compilation drawing on written records, chiefs, bards and family priests. Printed page references identify this uploaded edition. Recorded traditions, allegations and miracles are retained with their identities. All playable errands, spoken dialogue, choices and local outcomes are original adaptations, never claimed as verbatim testimony or actions historically performed by the fictional player roles. These recollections retain distinct periods rather than becoming one 1792 event.
source.scope: Foundational source for the first six sequences. Later court entries carry their own source_ids and references.

sequences.title: The Wedding Road
sequences.period: Late eighteenth century; Nakai marriage negotiations
sequences.adaptation: The source connects Bhagwan Singh's alliance through his sister with losses of territory and attempted interference. The errands, witnesses, dialogue and local outcomes are original. The prospective bride Raj Kaur is distinct from Ranjit Singh's mother.
sequences.opening: The courtyard is being dressed for visitors. Beyond its shade, horsemen wait beside bundles prepared for a marriage delegation. You are a household runner trusted with small tasks. Today those tasks bring you close to an alliance, and to someone determined to loosen it before the first greeting.

beats.objective: Inspect the gifts before the delegation leaves.
beats.line: The cloth is costly, but the message tied beneath it is worth more. The keeper asks whether every seal should be shown openly.

choices.label: Show every seal
choices.line: You lift the folded cloth so the witnesses can count the seals. Whatever follows, several households will remember what left this courtyard.

choices.label: Keep the letters covered
choices.line: You secure the letters beneath the gifts. The keeper accepts your discretion, although the people waiting outside must take your word for it.

beats.objective: Receive the delegate and agree how to enter.
beats.line: Our hosts will hear the names we speak first. Walk with me, and decide whether the introduction should stress kinship or the need for protection.

choices.label: Lead with kinship
choices.line: You answer that a household should hear a family greeting before a bargain. The delegate nods and follows you toward the entrance.

choices.label: Lead with protection
choices.line: You answer that exposed villages need an agreement with substance. The delegate gathers his attendants and follows you, prepared to speak plainly.

beats.objective: Escort the delegate across the courtyard to the entrance.
beats.line: At the entrance, a guard asks whose greeting he should announce. Behind you, the delegation waits for your account of the journey.

choices.label: Credit the whole escort
choices.line: You name the riders and attendants who brought the party safely. The announcement gives lesser companions a place in the story of this arrival.

choices.label: Name the sponsoring house
choices.line: You give the sponsoring household its full place in the announcement. The guard repeats it loudly enough for the gathering within to hear.

beats.objective: Hear the rival messenger before choosing whom to alert.
beats.line: A messenger steps out of the shade. He says the promises inside cannot be kept, and asks you to carry his warning without naming him.

choices.label: Report the interference
choices.line: You promise to repeat his words with their origin attached. His expression hardens; a private attempt to delay the alliance will now face witnesses.

choices.label: Ask what settlement he wants
choices.line: You ask what terms would end his interference. He offers no proof, but gives a demand the households can choose to answer.

beats.objective: Return to the keeper with your account of the arrival.
beats.line: The keeper listens while the sound of greetings rises beyond the entrance. Your errand is finished, but the household must decide what your discoveries mean.

choices.label: Name your witnesses
choices.line: You distinguish what you saw from what the messenger alleged, and name those who heard each part. The keeper can now question them directly.

choices.label: Keep the negotiation discreet
choices.line: You report the demand quietly and ask the keeper to leave room for an answer. The courtyard continues its preparations while the elders consider it.

endings.text: The delegation reaches its hosts under a public account. Named witnesses give the keeper a way to challenge the interference; the alliance remains a negotiation with consequences beyond this courtyard.
The greeting opens with kinship, and a rival demand reaches the elders without a public accusation. Your discretion leaves a narrow opportunity for accommodation.
The delegation has arrived. Your choices determine who received credit and how the rival message entered the household; the marriage negotiations continue beyond your small part in them.

sequences.title: The Unequal Victory
sequences.period: 1785; a remembered coalition and its strained aftermath
sequences.role: Fictional attendant to an allied contingent
sequences.location: A compressed gathering beside a disputed crossing
sequences.adaptation: The book records shifting Nakai, Sukerchakia and other chief relationships, the 1785 coalition after Jai Singh's 1783 seizure, and failed reconciliation. This local escort and honour dispute is invented to make those pressures playable.
sequences.opening: Dust has settled on a gathering of allied riders. They shared a campaign, but the welcome prepared for their return is uneven. You serve a smaller contingent whose wounded need passage and whose leader has noticed every slight. A successful errand may keep one conversation from becoming another quarrel.

beats.objective: Hear the captain's grievance before leaving the gathering.
beats.line: We rode beside them when the outcome was doubtful. Now their herald remembers only one household. Bring our people through before anyone answers an insult with steel.

choices.label: Promise to seek public credit
choices.line: You promise to speak to the herald after bringing the wounded through. The captain accepts a delay, expecting his people to be named.

choices.label: Promise the riders a safe passage
choices.line: You promise that every rider will reach the crossing before you discuss honour. The captain lets you go with a task that can be counted.

beats.objective: Ask the wounded companion how to make the passage.
beats.line: The crossing is close, but every step shakes my side. Let the banners pass if you must; just do not leave me beneath their horses.

choices.label: Walk together openly
choices.line: You ask the waiting riders to make space and place yourself beside your companion. He rises carefully and agrees to follow your pace.

choices.label: Take the quieter passage
choices.line: You point out a clear path beyond the waiting riders. Your companion follows, relieved that the passage will not become another public contest.

beats.objective: Escort the wounded companion to the crossing marker.
beats.line: At the marker, the far bank is visible. Your companion steadies himself and asks what you will tell the men who still wait behind.

choices.label: Ask both contingents for help
choices.line: You call for hands from both contingents. For a moment the work is simple: support a wounded rider and keep the path clear.

choices.label: Ask your own riders for help
choices.line: You call your own riders forward. They close around their companion, grateful that someone has remembered the obligation between them.

beats.objective: Challenge the victory announcement before it is repeated.
beats.line: The herald has already rehearsed the names. He can add the allied contingent, but asks whether you want its losses spoken before the assembled chiefs.

choices.label: Name the allies and their losses
choices.line: You ask him to name the allied riders and the cost they bore. The revised announcement gives their service a place the whole gathering can hear.

choices.label: Seek recognition in private
choices.line: You ask him to carry the request to the household quietly. He agrees to seek an audience, leaving the public announcement unchanged for now.

beats.objective: Decide how the remaining dressings should leave the gathering.
beats.line: There are fewer clean dressings than expected. The keeper can issue them by household or place them beside the crossing for whoever arrives wounded.

choices.label: Leave dressings at the crossing
choices.line: You ask for the bundles to be opened beside the passage. A rider from the other contingent takes the first strip and leaves the rest within reach.

choices.label: Reserve your contingent's share
choices.line: You count out the share owed to your own contingent. Its riders receive what they expected, while the remaining households must ask separately.

endings.text: The allies hear their service acknowledged, and their wounded share the same supplies. The rivalry remains, but this gathering ends with a small memory of mutual care.
Your contingent leaves with its people and supplies accounted for. Recognition is deferred to a private audience, carrying the captain's grievance into the next negotiation.
The wounded companion reaches the crossing. Your choices leave a particular account of honour and assistance; no errand can guarantee that today's allies remain allies tomorrow.

sequences.title: A Stranger at the Threshold
sequences.period: 1790; the book's account of revenge after Wazir Singh's death
sequences.role: Fictional attendant in Dal Singh's household
sequences.location: An exterior household court at Bahrwal
sequences.adaptation: The book attributes Wazir Singh's murder to Dal Singh, son of Hira Singh of Bahrwal, and says an unnamed devoted servant later killed Dal Singh in his household. The player witnesses warning signs and shelters people; choices do not cancel that recorded death or establish omniscient guilt.
sequences.opening: The household carries on beneath a silence nobody explains. A stranger waits near the entrance, asking after a man whose name makes the servants look away. You are an attendant with access to the yard and its families. You can decide where a warning travels, and who finds shelter before the disturbance comes.

beats.objective: Ask the stranger why he has come to the household.
beats.line: I have followed a name from one village to the next. Tell me where its owner sits, and you need trouble yourself no further.

choices.label: Ask whose service brought him
choices.line: You ask whose household he serves before offering directions. He gives no name, but his silence makes the errand feel older than today.

choices.label: Withhold the household's movements
choices.line: You say that visitors must speak to the steward. He studies the passage behind you; you leave him there without revealing who waits within.

beats.objective: Compare the stranger's account with the gate witness.
beats.line: He arrived alone and waited through two changes of guard. I heard Wazir Singh's name, but hearing a name does not tell me his purpose.

choices.label: Carry the witness's exact account
choices.line: You remember the name and the long wait, keeping them separate from your suspicions. The witness agrees to repeat those observations to the steward.

choices.label: Call attention to the danger
choices.line: You ask the gate witness to stay alert and call for help if the stranger moves inward. The waiting people turn toward your raised voice.

beats.objective: Warn the steward before the household gathering continues.
beats.line: The steward asks whether you bring an accusation or a warning. He has little time, and the people beyond the curtain have heard none of this.

choices.label: Deliver a warning with its limits
choices.line: You describe the stranger and the witness's words, then ask the steward to act before knowing more. He calls for attendants to watch the approaches.

choices.label: Ask permission to move dependents
choices.line: You ask first for the children and waiting relatives to be moved from the approach. The steward points you toward the shaded passage.

beats.objective: Bring the waiting dependent away from the approach.
beats.line: A young relative holds a bundle against her chest. She asks whether the gathering has ended, and whether the others know where she is going.

choices.label: Explain that you are finding shelter
choices.line: You tell her there may be trouble and that the shaded passage is safer. She keeps hold of the bundle and agrees to follow you.

choices.label: Keep the instructions calm and brief
choices.line: You ask her to walk with you and leave the entrance clear. She follows your measured voice while raised voices begin behind the curtain.

beats.objective: Escort the dependent into the sheltered passage.
beats.line: The passage narrows as a cry rises from the household. You cannot see its source. The person beside you asks whether she should go back.

choices.label: Keep her sheltered and call for aid
choices.line: You ask her to remain with you and call for attendants. The violence stays beyond your sight while you account for the people in your care.

choices.label: Keep her sheltered and send a witness
choices.line: You keep her beside you and ask a passing attendant to learn what happened. The household will need an account gathered from those who saw it.

endings.text: A dependent is sheltered and a witness is sought. The recollection closes with the book's account: Wazir Singh's devoted servant killed Dal Singh among his own household. Your actions preserve a local account, not an escape from that ending.

The warning reached the steward, and you brought a dependent out of the approach. The book's revenge still occurs beyond your sight; what survives your errand is a person sheltered and a warning remembered.
You remain beside the sheltered dependent as the household breaks into alarm. The narrator retains the book's fatal revenge, while your part concerns the people caught beside it.

sequences.title: Desi Remembers the Reins
sequences.role: Budha Singh in an explicitly dramatized family recollection
sequences.location: Open ground, a marked approach and a watering place
sequences.adaptation: The book names Budha Singh's piebald mare Desi and credits him with surviving about forty wounds. This short ride, horse responses and dialogue are original. It preserves the larger-than-life ancestor without treating the ride as a documented journey.
sequences.opening: Before the household becomes a genealogy, there is a rider and a piebald mare. The family calls her Desi. In this ancestral recollection, Budha Singh must guide her from the waiting ground to water. The narrator remembers wounds and endurance; the player discovers the partnership through a quieter act of riding.

beats.objective: Approach Desi and take the saddle.
beats.line: She watches your hands before she moves her feet. The old companion waits beside the path, giving rider and mare a moment to understand each other.

choices.label: Let her settle before mounting
choices.line: You give Desi time to stand, then take the saddle without hurrying her. Her ears turn toward the open approach as you gather the reins.

choices.label: Mount with the familiar signal
choices.line: You touch the saddle and give the familiar signal before mounting. Desi steps beneath your weight as though this small ceremony has happened a hundred times.

beats.objective: Ride Desi to the first route marker.
beats.line: The ground opens ahead. Her stride lengthens beneath you, then shortens when your hands settle. Beyond the marker, the route turns toward the watering place.

choices.label: Keep a measured stride
choices.line: You guide her through the marker at an even pace. Each step leaves you room to read the ground and prepare for the next turn.

choices.label: Give her room to find her stride
choices.line: You ease your hands and let her find the line through the open ground. The route remains yours to choose, but she carries its rhythm.

beats.objective: Ride at least twelve metres before reaching the far marker.
beats.line: At the far marker, the mare answers the turn without a struggle. The companion's voice carries after you, speaking of journeys whose names the family still remembers.

choices.label: Read the ground before returning
choices.line: You pause to read the lower ground and choose the clear approach to water. Desi waits beneath you while the dust settles around her feet.

choices.label: Answer the companion across the ground
choices.line: You call back that the mare has brought you through cleanly. The companion laughs, pleased that her part in the journey has been acknowledged.

beats.objective: Reach the watering place and dismount beside Desi.
beats.line: Water darkens the edge of the trough. Whatever battles the teller will give this rider, the mare still needs a quiet hand and time to drink.

choices.label: Let Desi drink before speaking
choices.line: You dismount and loosen your hold so Desi can lower her head. The companion waits while the small sounds of drinking fill the pause.

choices.label: Check her tack before the rest
choices.line: You dismount and check the tack, easing what has pulled during the ride. When you lead her to water, she follows without needing another signal.

beats.objective: Return to the companion and choose what the story remembers.
beats.line: The companion says a family may count a warrior's wounds until it forgets the days between them. He asks what should be remembered of this ride.

choices.label: Remember the mare beside the rider
choices.line: You ask him to remember Desi's patience and the ground she carried you over. In the telling, the horse keeps her name beside the ancestor.

choices.label: Remember the endurance of the pair
choices.line: You ask him to remember that both rider and mare returned. The larger tale can carry its wounds and victories around that simple image.

endings.text: The recollection closes with Desi drinking and the companion carrying her name into the story. A legendary ancestor gains an intimate memory: someone who learned when to wait for his horse.
The family remembers the rider's endurance, and Desi remains beside him in that image. The ride supplies an authored moment of companionship within the recorded ancestral tradition.
You complete the ride and return to the companion. Desi keeps her place in the family story, with the care and pace you chose along the way.

sequences.title: What Can Be Carried
sequences.period: Late eighteenth century; Ramgarhia displacement and return traditions
sequences.role: Fictional attendant among displaced Ramgarhia followers
sequences.location: A compressed roadside halt outside a hospitable settlement
sequences.adaptation: The source contains Ramgarhia humiliation, release with gifts, retaliatory vows, exile and a treasure-in-a-well episode. This relief errand and its choices are original, with the treasure retained as narrated possibility rather than a fabricated documented discovery by the player.
sequences.opening: The estate lies behind you, but its people have not vanished. They wait beside bundles that were packed too quickly, looking toward a settlement whose welcome is uncertain. You serve a displaced party. Before anyone can speak of returning, someone must secure a place to rest and decide what promises can honestly be made.

beats.objective: Hear the elder before seeking shelter for the party.
beats.line: They speak of returning before they have counted who came away. Take our names to the settlement. A promise is useful only if someone remains to keep it.

choices.label: Promise an account of every person
choices.line: You ask the elder to count names while you seek shelter. The work gives the waiting party something firmer than another promise of revenge.

choices.label: Carry the household's vow of return
choices.line: You agree to carry the household's intention to return, while asking the elder to keep the party together. The vow travels with an immediate obligation.

beats.objective: Choose what the salvaged supplies can offer the hosts.
beats.line: Among the bundles are blankets and a few goods that can be exchanged. Every gift buys goodwill, but every gift also leaves somebody carrying less.

choices.label: Offer goods for the night's shelter
choices.line: You set aside goods the party can spare and keep the blankets for its tired people. The offer gives your request a tangible answer.

choices.label: Keep the goods and offer service
choices.line: You leave the bundles together and prepare an offer of work. Shelter will create an obligation the party must remember after the immediate danger passes.

beats.objective: Negotiate a night's hospitality with the settlement host.
beats.line: The host has heard about the quarrel and fears it may arrive behind you. She asks whether shelter today will make her household an enemy tomorrow.

choices.label: Ask for shelter with a limited promise
choices.line: You ask only for a night and promise that your party will respect the settlement's stores. She grants space while keeping her own people nearby.

choices.label: Promise to remember the hospitality
choices.line: You offer future help in return for tonight's welcome. She agrees, asking you to remember the names of those who make room.

beats.objective: Gather the weary follower for the last walk to shelter.
beats.line: A follower has heard that fortune was once found in a well. He asks whether the tale means your people are destined to rise again.

choices.label: Let the treasure tale sustain him
choices.line: You let him finish the story, then point toward the shelter already secured. He rises to follow, carrying the possibility of fortune with him.

choices.label: Name the help already within reach
choices.line: You say that tonight's host has already changed the party's fortune. He rises to follow, still keeping his well story for another evening.

beats.objective: Escort the weary follower to the shelter entrance.
beats.line: At the entrance, the waiting party begins to settle. Beyond them lies the road home, still closed, while the host waits to hear how you will remember tonight.

choices.label: Thank the hosts before speaking of return
choices.line: You name the people who made space and let the party rest before repeating its ambitions. The memory of exile gains a household that offered shelter.

choices.label: Renew the vow with an obligation to the hosts
choices.line: You repeat the vow of return and add the names of those who sheltered you. Whatever comes later, the vow now carries a debt of hospitality.

endings.text: The displaced party finds shelter through a limited promise and a remembered welcome. The road back remains a future story; tonight its people have somewhere to sleep.
The vow of return survives beside the well-treasure tradition. It now carries the names of hosts who helped when power and possessions could not.
You bring the follower into shelter. The party keeps its losses, vows and stories, with a new obligation to the people who opened their settlement.

sequences.title: The Water of Bahrwal
sequences.period: Ancestral legend; Guru Arjun and Hem Raj
sequences.role: Fictional attendant witnessing a narrated family legend
sequences.location: Open well and exterior household threshold at Bahrwal
sequences.adaptation: The book records Hem Raj carrying the sleeping Guru Arjun home on a charpai, brackish water becoming sweet, and a blessing promising a powerful descendant. This adaptation preserves the miracle as the legend tells it. Dialogue and attendant errands are original; no Guru avatar, impersonation or religious-building entry is required.
sequences.opening: The storyteller brings you to Bahrwal before its later chiefs. Beside the open well, an attendant has drawn water that tastes brackish. The tale says Hem Raj finds Guru Arjun asleep, carries him home upon the charpai, and receives a blessing. You follow the hospitality surrounding that moment, while the legend unfolds in the narrator's voice.

beats.objective: Draw the first water from the Bahrwal well.
beats.line: The bucket returns heavy, but the water tastes brackish. In the family's telling, the same well will soon become the place by which a blessing is remembered.

choices.label: Tell the household how the water tastes
choices.line: You carry your observation openly: there is water, but it is brackish. The household must decide how to welcome a guest with what it has.

choices.label: Carry the water with care
choices.line: You keep the bucket steady and bring what the well has given. The teller lingers on the ordinary labour that makes a welcome possible.

beats.objective: Prepare the household's welcome from the open courtyard.
beats.line: The attendant asks for a clear threshold and a place to set the water. Hospitality must be ready before anyone knows what this visit will mean.

choices.label: Prepare a clear approach
choices.line: You make room along the approach and ask others to keep it open. The household's attention turns toward receiving the sleeping guest without disturbance.

choices.label: Set the water within reach
choices.line: You place the water where it can be offered and wait for the household's signal. Nothing in this small task tells you how the story will be remembered.

beats.objective: Reach the resting-place marker and hear the charpai episode.
beats.line: The narrator tells how Hem Raj finds Guru Arjun asleep and carries him home upon the charpai. The quiet journey becomes an act the family will remember.

choices.label: Follow the narrated passage quietly
choices.line: You listen as the teller carries the scene from resting place to household. The sleeping guest remains in the telling; your footsteps follow its remembered route.

choices.label: Attend to Hem Raj's act of service
choices.line: You hold your attention on the care of the carrying. The teller makes space for that effort before speaking of what followed at the well.

beats.objective: Listen at the exterior threshold as the blessing is told.
beats.line: At the household threshold, the narrator gives the blessing its full place: a powerful descendant is promised, and the well's brackish water becomes sweet.

choices.label: Receive the legend as the household tells it
choices.line: You let the promise stand in the family's own telling. The household, its descendant and the changing water are joined within one remembered act of hospitality.

choices.label: Remember the blessing through the well
choices.line: You fix the well in memory as the place where the blessing can be retold. The narrator keeps both the promised descendant and the sweetened water.

beats.objective: Return to the well and draw its sweetened water.
beats.line: In the legend, the bucket now rises with sweet water. The teller returns to the same ordinary movement, giving it a meaning the first drawing could not hold.

choices.label: Share the sweet water with the household
choices.line: You bring the sweet water back toward the waiting household. The miracle remains whole in the tale, carried through the same hands that first drew brackish water.

choices.label: Carry the well's story onward
choices.line: You pause beside the well and repeat the sequence to its keeper: hospitality, blessing, sweet water and the promise of a descendant whose name will matter.

endings.text: The family legend closes with water shared. Hem Raj's hospitality, Guru Arjun's blessing and the promise of a powerful descendant remain together in the tale, with the miracle preserved.
The well holds the story: brackish water, the sleeping guest carried home, a blessing, sweet water and a powerful descendant promised. Your role has been to follow and carry that legend.
The narrator leaves Bahrwal with its miracle intact. The open well becomes a remembered place through which the household tells its ancestry.

sequences.title: The Door to the Young Chief
sequences.role: Fictional adult clerk of the Sukerchakia household
sequences.location: An exterior audience court at Gujranwala
sequences.adaptation: The Memorial records Lakhpat Rai quarrelling with Dal Singh, Maha Singh's maternal uncle, and a temporary reconciliation. Buxi supplies the household power struggle. The user-selected 1792 frame retains the project chronology beside the Memorial's 1790 succession. Sada's participation in this particular access dispute and all dialogue are original adaptations of the supplied political plot. This Dal is the elder regency figure, distinct from Dal son of Hira Singh of Bahrwal, killed in the revenge account.
sequences.opening: Three people wait for one door to open. Lakhpat Rai has the account books. Dal Singh has the authority of kinship. Sada Kaur has arrived with an answer of her own. You hold the audience list, and every person in the court understands that the order of names can become an order of power.

beats.objective: Receive Lakhpat Rai's order for the audience list.
beats.line: Lakhpat Rai: A household cannot spend the same rupee twice. Put the accounts before the petitions, and let those who demand soldiers explain how they will feed them.

choices.label: Give the accounts first place
choices.line: You put the accounts at the head of the list. Lakhpat closes the ledger with satisfaction, while a waiting petitioner watches his own name move downward.

choices.label: Reserve time for the petitions
choices.line: You give the ledger its place but mark an hour for petitions. Lakhpat studies the additional line before allowing the register back into your hands.

beats.objective: Hear Dal Singh's objection at the waiting place.
beats.line: Dal Singh: I knew this family before a clerk could admit me to it. If Lakhpat speaks for its wealth, someone must speak for its obligations.

choices.label: Record his objection beside his name
choices.line: You enter the objection without erasing the Diwan's place. Dal agrees that the young chief should hear the disagreement, although he dislikes having to wait.

choices.label: Propose that both men be heard together
choices.line: You suggest a joint hearing, with neither account presented behind the other's back. Dal permits you to carry the proposal, reserving his answer until he hears Lakhpat's.

beats.objective: Receive Sada Kaur and choose how to announce her arrival.
beats.line: Sada Kaur: They argue over who holds the door. I would know what waits beyond it. Take me in, and leave enough room for the boy to answer.

choices.label: Announce her openly before entering
choices.line: You tell the waiting court that Sada Kaur is approaching the audience. She follows without hurrying, allowing every face to see who has chosen to accompany her.

choices.label: Take her in after a quiet notice
choices.line: You send a quiet notice ahead and ask the waiting men to keep the approach clear. Sada follows, with her arrival known before her intentions are.

beats.objective: Escort Sada Kaur to the audience entrance.
beats.line: At the threshold, an attendant asks whether Dal Singh and Lakhpat should enter together. Their quarrel can be heard here, or continue through messages outside.

choices.label: Call both men into the hearing
choices.line: You ask the attendant to admit both men in the same announcement. The order creates a meeting neither can later describe as having excluded him.

choices.label: Keep the scheduled separate hearings
choices.line: You ask the attendant to keep the appointments as written. Each man will have his interval to speak, and each will wonder what the other said.

beats.objective: Complete the audience register after the door closes.
beats.line: The court grows quiet enough to hear the reed pen. Your final line will tell tomorrow's attendants whether today ended a quarrel or merely interrupted it.

choices.label: Record a temporary working agreement
choices.line: You write that the accounts and petitions will both be heard, with the existing appointments retained for now. The words leave room for tomorrow's disagreement.

choices.label: Preserve the objections beside the agreement
choices.line: You preserve both objections beneath the working agreement. No name disappears, and anyone reopening the matter must confront what was said in this court.

endings.text: Both men entered the same hearing, and the register records a temporary agreement. You have secured an interval in which the household can act, while preserving the reasons its elders disagree.
The appointments remain separate, and the objections remain on the page. Your orderly register carries the rivalry forward without pretending that a closed door has settled it.
The audience begins and the household has a written order for its business. Your route through the court decides whose authority was displayed and whose objection survives the day.

sequences.title: The Whisper After Midnight
sequences.role: Fictional adult attendant carrying a household report
sequences.location: A lamp-lit outer court at Gujranwala
sequences.adaptation: Griffin repeats allegations about Raj Kaur, Lakhpat Rai and matricide, then doubts the killing stories. Buxi describes the struggle over authority and cites Sinha's rejection of Smyth's accusation. Neither establishes guilt. This night, its letter, the witnesses and every spoken line are invented. Poison remains an allegation voiced by a character, never an acquired poison item or biological finding. Timing is deliberately broad; no death in 1801 is asserted.
sequences.opening: A lamp is still burning where the household has ordered darkness. Someone says the room was locked. Someone else says poison. Between those two statements, a frightened attendant has become a person everyone wants to question. You must bring her across the court before the story reaches the gate without her.

beats.objective: Hear what the waiting messenger intends to repeat.
beats.line: Messenger: They are saying the mother drank poison, and that the order came from above. If I wait for permission, every rival household will hear another man's version first.

choices.label: Ask where his account began
choices.line: You ask him to name the person who spoke first. His certainty softens into a chain of other voices, none of whom stood beside the cup.

choices.label: Ask him to wait for the attendant
choices.line: You ask him to stay until the attendant has spoken. He complains that delay looks like concealment, but accepts that a living voice may alter the message.

beats.objective: Examine the unsigned account before it leaves the court.
beats.line: The sheet names Raj Kaur and Lakhpat Rai, then changes from events to accusations without a new line. Its writer has left no signature.

choices.label: Mark the accusations as unconfirmed
choices.line: You mark where the account moves beyond a witnessed event. The sheet still carries the allegations, but its next reader will see the change in certainty.

choices.label: Keep the sheet intact for the hearing
choices.line: You fold the sheet without changing it. Preserving the whole accusation may expose its author's intention, provided someone asks who wrote it.

beats.objective: Hear the attendant before taking her away from the gathering.
beats.line: Attendant: I saw the door shut. I heard an argument. That is all. They keep asking what was in the cup as though fear could make me remember it.

choices.label: Promise a private hearing
choices.line: You promise to bring her to a sheltered place before taking her account. She follows because the promise concerns where she will speak, not what she must say.

choices.label: Promise that others will hear her accurately
choices.line: You promise that her exact words will be heard by more than one person. She follows, asking you to stay if someone tries to finish her sentences.

beats.objective: Escort the attendant to the sheltered passage.
beats.line: At the passage, a guard wants her name for his list. She stops beside you, suddenly more afraid of being recorded than of the darkness behind.

choices.label: Ask that her name stay within the hearing
choices.line: You give the guard enough to admit her and ask that her name remain with the hearing. He agrees to keep curious messengers outside.

choices.label: Record her presence with protection requested
choices.line: You enter her presence and request protection against pressure. The record makes her visible to authority, with your own name beside the request.

beats.objective: Choose how the night register will carry the accusation.
beats.line: Keeper: I can seal this for an inquiry, or read the accusation before the assembled household. Either way, people will ask why you chose it.

choices.label: Seal it for a private inquiry
choices.line: You seal the account with the attendant's limited statement. The poison allegation remains inside, waiting beside the words of someone who will not claim to have seen it.

choices.label: Read the allegation and its limits publicly
choices.line: You read the accusation aloud, then state what the attendant actually witnessed. The gathering hears both, although you cannot control which part people carry away.

endings.text: The attendant reaches shelter and the accusation enters a sealed inquiry. The court keeps its troubling story, while one person is protected from being forced to supply its missing certainty.
The accusation becomes public beside the attendant's narrower account. You have preserved her words, but their limits must now travel through a household hungry for a culprit.
The attendant reaches the passage and the report is delivered. Nothing you carried proves poison or guilt; your choices determine how a dangerous allegation enters the household's memory.

sequences.title: Two Names in the Dispatch
sequences.role: Fictional adult courier of the Batala household
sequences.location: An exterior household court at Batala
source_pages: Centenary Memorial: printed 25 / PDF 45; printed 251–252 / PDF 291–292
sequences.adaptation: Griffin alleges substituted children and later political acknowledgement; the Memorial records the twins' birth announcement, thanksgiving and Mehtab's maternity. Neither the courier nor the choices establish biological truth. All dialogue, dispatch handling and minor witnesses are original. The scene preserves competing accusations without encoding strict male primogeniture or deciding future accession. Its authored 1807 frame follows the selected announcement variant and does not silently reconcile every source chronology.
sequences.opening: Two names have been written before the dispatch is dry. Beyond the courtyard curtain, the household prepares a celebration. At the gate, another story is already waiting to travel. You have been asked to carry the announcement to Ranjit Singh, and every person you meet wants a different sentence placed beside it.

beats.objective: Receive the household announcement from Mehtab Kaur's steward.
beats.line: Steward: Sher Singh and Tara Singh. Write the names clearly. My mistress asks that the message reach their father before the courtyard begins answering questions from strangers.

choices.label: Put the names before political titles
choices.line: You place the children's names at the beginning and leave the household's requested address intact. The dispatch starts with people before it reaches the question of rank.

choices.label: Preserve the household's full formal address
choices.line: You retain every formal address requested by the household. The wording carries its claim with dignity, without giving you the authority to decide how it will be received.

beats.objective: Hear Sada Kaur's instruction before sealing the message.
beats.line: Sada Kaur: A rumour can cross a courtyard faster than a horse crosses a field. Carry our announcement with your own eyes open, and do not let another man write your arrival.

choices.label: Ask for an acknowledged delivery
choices.line: You ask for instructions to obtain a named receipt at the other end. Sada agrees that no officer should be able to deny the message arrived.

choices.label: Ask to deliver the words before witnesses
choices.line: You ask to read the announcement before witnesses if access is granted. Sada permits it, knowing that a public arrival can also invite a public refusal.

beats.objective: Decide how the dispatch should carry the competing allegation.
beats.line: A second slip alleges that a weaver's child and another child were brought into the household. It offers no witness who will travel with you.

choices.label: Keep the accusation in a separate marked enclosure
choices.line: You place the allegation in a separate enclosure marked as an unsupported report. The announcement remains whole, while the recipient can inspect what is being said against it.

choices.label: Leave the unsigned allegation with the steward
choices.line: You leave the unsigned slip for the steward to investigate. Your dispatch carries the entrusted announcement, and the allegation retains a place where someone may seek its author.

beats.objective: Gather the escort rider before leaving Batala.
beats.line: Rider: At the first halt someone will ask what we carry. Tell me what I am allowed to answer, and I will keep to those words.

choices.label: Permit only the birth announcement
choices.line: You tell him to repeat the two names and that the household has sent an announcement. He follows, with no authority to embellish the message.

choices.label: Keep the dispatch private until delivery
choices.line: You ask him to say only that you carry a household dispatch. He follows, understanding that privacy may protect the message and also invite speculation.

beats.objective: Escort the rider to the departure entrance with the dispatch.
beats.line: The gatekeeper offers to enter the journey as a celebration or as confidential service. Your companion waits beside the sealed packet while the road brightens beyond the wall.

choices.label: Register a household birth announcement
choices.line: You register the journey as a birth announcement entrusted by the household. Its arrival can be checked without turning the gatebook into a verdict on descent.

choices.label: Register confidential household service
choices.line: You register confidential service and name the sender and receiving office. The message has a traceable journey while its contents remain with its keepers.

endings.text: The birth announcement leaves Batala with a separate allegation and a requested receipt. You have kept two competing claims from becoming one sentence; the courier's journey cannot settle what the court will believe.

The household's announcement leaves under confidential service, while the unsigned accusation remains with the steward. Your restraint protects the entrusted message, but it cannot silence the story waiting at the gate.
Two names leave Batala in a sealed dispatch. Your choices shape the manner of delivery and the reach of the allegation, without deciding the children's descent or their later political fortunes.

sequences.title: The Fortress in the Letter
sequences.role: Fictional adult courier entrusted by Sada Kaur
sequences.location: A compressed exterior dispatch court near Atalgarh
source_pages: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Sada Kaur entry, secret British negotiations
Discover Sikhism: Sardarni Sada Kaur, paragraph beginning In November 1808
sequences.adaptation: The university entry records secret negotiations with British officers. Discover Sikhism describes a November 1808 offer of Atalgarh to Metcalfe tied to restoration of possessions. The packet, route, receiving agent and conditions voiced here are invented. This stage ends with an approach delivered, never a completed alliance, an invented interception or a transfer of the fort. Atalgarh here belongs to Sada's diplomatic story, not Dal Singh's Akalgarh identity.
sequences.opening: A fortress has become a line in a folded letter. Around you, its people continue counting grain and opening the morning gate. You carry an approach to an outside power, but the receiving agent has promised only to listen. Before the packet leaves your hands, you must decide what record its journey will leave behind.

beats.objective: Receive Sada Kaur's instruction for the sealed approach.
beats.line: Sada Kaur: They count my walls when they speak of my loyalty. Let them consider what those walls are worth, and what it would cost to leave their keeper unheard.

choices.label: Ask that restoration remain the first condition
choices.line: You ask her to place the restoration of her position before every practical offer. She agrees that the receiving party must hear a condition, not an unconditional gift.

choices.label: Ask for a hearing before practical promises
choices.line: You ask for a hearing before anyone measures stores or billets. She agrees to send the approach as an opening whose next terms must still be answered.

beats.objective: Consult the storekeeper before carrying any practical assurance.
beats.line: Storekeeper: A visiting officer will see empty ground and call it room for his men. I see families, carts and grain already promised elsewhere. Which account will travel?

choices.label: Include the existing obligations in your oral account
choices.line: You undertake to describe the people and stores already committed here. The storekeeper gives you the names of those whose work a casual promise might displace.

choices.label: Give no capacity figures without a written request
choices.line: You promise no figures from memory and ask him to prepare a written inventory if requested. He keeps his book closed until a definite question arrives.

beats.objective: Secure the packet and choose its delivery record.
beats.line: The outer wrapper bears a receiving name, while the inner fold remains sealed. Beside it lies space for a date, a witness and an answer that has not come.

choices.label: Record the intact seal before handing it over
choices.line: You record the seal's condition with the packet still on the table. A later denial of receipt must now answer an account made before the exchange.

choices.label: Ask a household witness to record your departure
choices.line: You ask an attendant to record the packet leaving in your care. The contents remain concealed, but your own responsibility begins in another person's sight.

beats.objective: Meet the receiving agent and establish the limit of his authority.
beats.line: Agent: I can carry an approach. I cannot promise protection, troops or an answer. Walk with me to the gate, and say plainly what acknowledgement you require.

choices.label: Require a receipt for delivery alone
choices.line: You ask for a receipt that acknowledges delivery without pretending agreement. The agent accepts those terms and follows you toward the outer entrance.

choices.label: Require a named route for the reply
choices.line: You ask him to name the office through which a reply can return. He supplies that route and follows, while keeping every political promise outside his answer.

beats.objective: Escort the agent to the outer entrance and complete the handoff.
beats.line: At the entrance, the agent turns once more toward the fort. Nothing has changed hands except a packet, but the keeper of the gate asks what he should report.

choices.label: Report that an approach has been delivered
choices.line: You report the delivery and leave the response open. The gatekeeper enters a completed journey, while the political meaning remains for those who must answer it.

choices.label: Report the conditions repeated at handoff
choices.line: You report which conditions were repeated and which promises were withheld. The gatekeeper records an exchange whose limits may matter as much as its offer.

endings.text: The agent leaves with a packet, an acknowledged delivery and a record of existing obligations. The approach remains open; the people who occupy the fort have not disappeared into the language of an offer.
The courier has a route for a reply and a clear account of the conditions. A guarded opening has been made, with neither protection nor possession awarded by your handoff.
The diplomatic packet crosses the outer entrance. Your record distinguishes the journey you completed from the agreement its sender hopes may follow.

sequences.title: Behind the Lowered Curtain
sequences.role: Fictional adult retainer serving Sada Kaur
sequences.location: A compressed night camp and outer entrance
source_pages: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Sada Kaur entry, covered-litter escape
Discover Sikhism: Sardarni Sada Kaur, paragraph beginning But instead of giving fresh jagirs
sequences.adaptation: Griffin and the university entry preserve a covered-litter escape followed by detention. Discover Sikhism dates its account to 1820 and names Vasakha Singh as the informing retainer and Desa Singh as the pursuer. This 1820–1821 frame retains chronology variants. The player is a fictional additional retainer; dialogue, papers and movement choices are original. Detention is fixed. Local agency determines the treatment of bearers, the wording of a report and how the party reaches its last gate, never a successful alternate escape.
sequences.opening: The curtain has been lowered before the lamps are put out. The bearers know they have been called for a journey nobody wishes to announce. Somewhere beyond the camp, a horse is being saddled. You serve the woman inside the litter, and your smallest instruction may decide who is blamed when the road closes.

stations.label: Travel papers and a small bundle

beats.objective: Receive Sada Kaur's instruction before the curtain is lowered.
beats.line: Sada Kaur: I have heard enough advice spoken over my possessions. Bring the bearers quietly. Whatever another man calls this journey tomorrow, tonight I intend to choose its first step.

choices.label: Promise that the bearers will not be coerced
choices.line: You promise to explain the immediate journey to the bearers and let them name their concerns. She allows it, impatient with delay but unwilling to begin with a quarrel.

choices.label: Promise a discreet departure without a false order
choices.line: You promise to keep the departure quiet without inventing a command in another person's name. She gives a short nod and asks you to be quick.

beats.objective: Choose what account of the departure to leave with the papers.
beats.line: A travel wrapper lies open beside the bundle. It can carry the household's request as spoken, or a brief account of who received the instruction.

choices.label: Leave the household's request in writing
choices.line: You leave a plain account that the household requested a journey. The paper gives no false promise of permission and places no order in the bearers' mouths.

choices.label: Record your own responsibility for the preparations
choices.line: You put your own role in the preparations on the sheet. If someone later searches for a convenient culprit, the bearers need not stand alone.

beats.objective: Confront Vasakha Singh before returning to the bearers.
beats.line: Vasakha Singh: Every road out of this camp returns to someone's account of it. I have sent my word. If yours differs, make certain you can defend it when the riders arrive.

choices.label: Ask him to distinguish departure from armed defiance
choices.line: You ask that his account distinguish a departure from an armed challenge. He gives no promise to stop the riders, but hears the difference you insist upon.

choices.label: Ask him to name the bearers as hired workers
choices.line: You ask him to make clear that the bearers carry a passenger rather than command a faction. He agrees to mention their position in his account.

beats.objective: Gather the bearers and begin the short approach to the gate.
beats.line: Bearer: Once we lift, we cannot set her down at every shout. Tell us whether to stop at the first guard, or keep together until the entrance.

choices.label: Keep everyone together and stop for a clear challenge
choices.line: You ask the bearers to stay together and stop if a guard gives a clear challenge. They lift carefully and follow your pace toward the entrance.

choices.label: Keep the litter together until the entrance
choices.line: You ask them to keep the party together through the open court. They lift and follow, knowing that a scattered group would be easier to accuse.

beats.objective: Escort the covered litter to the outer camp entrance.
beats.line: The entrance closes before the party can pass. Riders have brought an order to return. Behind the curtain there is a long silence, and the bearers wait for your voice.

choices.label: Acknowledge the order and demand a recorded return
choices.line: You acknowledge the order and ask the guard to record who returns under it. The bearers lower their burden carefully while you remain beside the litter.

choices.label: State a protest and name everyone placed in custody
choices.line: You state the household's protest, then name the people being taken back. The gate stays closed, but the return begins with an account that includes its witnesses.

endings.text: The party is detained. Your account separates the hired bearers from the political dispute and records the return, preserving a small measure of protection when you cannot reopen the road.
The gate remains closed and the detention proceeds. You have put your own responsibility beside a named protest, so the last part of this journey cannot be told entirely without its attendants.
Sada Kaur is taken back into detention. Your choices shape the report and the treatment of the people beside her; the closed road remains part of the recollection's fixed ending.

sequences.title: When the Camp Falls Quiet
sequences.role: Fictional young runner serving a veteran of Maha Singh's household
sequences.location: A compressed Sodhra camp and evacuation gate
sequences.adaptation: This scene selects Griffin's 1792 illness and withdrawal, not the Memorial's 1790 child-victory outcome. The father's private words, delegated tasks, veteran, young runner, evacuation staging and choices are original drama. Authority passes through a small order to care for the camp; this is not evidence for a documented bedside investiture. Maha's death after his return remains fixed. Mana Singh is a research lead, not the identity assigned to the fictional veteran.
sequences.opening: A moment ago, men shouted over one another to be heard by the chief. Now every voice has dropped. Maha Singh sits beneath the shelter, trying to hide the shaking in his hands. His son waits outside. The veteran who sent you for water has served this household longer than you have been alive; for the first time, he does not know what to tell the boy.

beats.objective: Receive the father's order before the camp moves.
beats.line: Maha steadies the cup against his knee. "My son thinks I cannot hear him outside. Tell him I heard every question. Then tell him this: nobody leaves the camp forgotten. He can begin with that."

choices.label: Carry his exact words
choices.line: You repeat the order back. Maha closes his eyes, then opens them when you reach the last sentence. "Yes. That one matters."

choices.label: Ask who will stand beside his son
choices.line: "The men who stood beside me," Maha says. "A boy may need an answer twice. Let them have the patience to give it." You ask the veteran to hear this himself.

beats.objective: Bring the veteran into the evacuation work.
beats.line: The veteran rolls his sleeve and takes the cord for the waiting bearers. "I have followed his orders through worse noise than this. It is the quiet I cannot bear. Come. His boy must see us doing something useful."

choices.label: Admit that you are frightened
choices.line: "Good," he says softly. "Then we shall count twice." He asks you to walk beside him while he checks the passage.

choices.label: Ask how Maha first trusted him
choices.line: He smiles without looking up. "With a task too small to boast about, and too necessary to neglect. Much like yours." He takes his place beside you.

beats.objective: Escort the veteran to the evacuation gate.
beats.line: The opening is crowded with people waiting for instructions. The veteran raises an empty hand. "Make room. We are bringing our chief home. The rest of you are coming home with him."

choices.label: Count attendants and dependents
choices.line: You call for the people behind the bundles to answer by name. A cook returns for a helper who has been waiting for someone to notice him.

choices.label: Leave a witness at the gate
choices.line: You ask a trusted attendant to remain until each departing group has been heard from. The veteran makes the same promise aloud: nobody shuts this gate early.

beats.objective: Prepare what the returning party needs.
beats.line: A clean cloth lies beside the last covered water jar. The keeper looks toward the shelter. "For him, or for the bearers? Say it plainly. I cannot fill an empty jar with respect."

choices.label: Divide the water between chief and bearers
choices.line: You fill the chief's cup, then portion the remainder for the people carrying him. The keeper ties a cloth around the jar so another hand can find it quickly.

choices.label: Request the household's reserved jar
choices.line: You ask the keeper to open the household reserve and take responsibility for the request. He sends an attendant for it; the chief's portion can now remain beside him.

beats.objective: Give Ranjit his father's message.
beats.line: The boy has been watching the gate. "Everyone tells me what my father ordered," he says. "Did he ask for me?" Beyond the shelter, the veteran waits for your answer.

choices.label: Tell him his father heard him
choices.line: You give the private words before the camp order. His face changes at the first sentence. "Then I will ask him again when we reach home." He turns to help count the departing groups.

choices.label: Ask him to check the camp with the veteran
choices.line: You give the order and bring the veteran forward. "Your father trusted me with many things," the older man tells him. "Today he has trusted us with the same thing."

endings.text: The boy carries his father's words into the thinning camp. The attendants answer one by one, and the departure begins with their names accounted for. You have changed how this household leaves Sodhra, not the father's approaching death.

The veteran stands beside the young heir while the gate clears. Their first shared duty is small enough to finish: bring the waiting people through. The authority being inherited already has faces attached to it.

The camp empties toward Gujranwala. The boy watches the bearers carry his father home, with the veteran walking beside them. Maha Singh will not return to this field; the people leaving it have begun to look toward his son.

sequences.title: Names at the Gate
sequences.role: Fictional young retainer assisting a household veteran
sequences.location: A compressed reception courtyard outside Rasulnagar/Ramnagar
sequences.adaptation: The entry takes the reported estates and military employment offered to Jan Muhammad's sons as its historical anchor. The unnamed family representative, veteran, clerk, guarantees, supplies, dialogue and local outcomes are original. These people speak for particular households, never every Chattha family. The sequence follows the conflict without replaying its killing; jobs and provision do not erase bereavement. The late-1790s period is separate from the 1792 opening.
sequences.opening: The courtyard gate is open, but the visitors have stopped outside it. A clerk waits with the terms of a grant and an offer of service. The eldest visitor keeps looking at the covered bundles brought from his household. You have been sent to bring him in. The veteran beside you knows that an open gate and a promise of safety are not yet the same thing.

beats.objective: Learn what you may promise the waiting family.
beats.line: "Bring them to hear the terms," the veteran says. "Do not promise their grief will end when the clerk closes his book. And if you give your word about this gate, stay here to keep it."

choices.label: Establish who can guarantee passage
choices.line: You ask whose word the gatekeepers will obey. The veteran names himself and agrees to stand where the visitors can see him.

choices.label: Ask what the household needs first
choices.line: The veteran points toward the bundles. "Ask them. We have already done enough deciding what they ought to want."

beats.objective: Hear the representative before entering together.
beats.line: "They have written our names beside an estate and a place in service," the visitor says. "Have they written the names of those who must eat while we consider it? My family has come for an answer, not a celebration."

choices.label: Hear the dependents' needs first
choices.line: You ask him to name who remains at home and what cannot wait. He gives you a short list, then agrees to walk beside you to the clerk.

choices.label: Hear his questions about service first
choices.line: You ask what must be made clear before anyone accepts service. "Who calls us, and who hears us if the promise is broken." He follows you toward the entrance.

beats.objective: Escort the representative through the reception gate.
beats.line: A gatekeeper asks the visitor to wait while the household is announced. He stops at once. "A moment ago you asked me to trust the road. Now I must trust the doorway too?"

choices.label: Call the veteran forward as guarantor
choices.line: You call the veteran by his role and ask him to repeat the passage promise before both parties. The gatekeeper steps aside only after hearing it.

choices.label: Remain beside the visitor while waiting
choices.line: You stay at his side and send the announcement ahead. When permission returns, you both pass through the same opening, at the same pace.

beats.objective: Ask the clerk to state what provision and service require.
beats.line: The clerk reads the proposed grant and employment aloud. The visitor listens without sitting. "An estate has boundaries. An obligation should have them too. Tell me where each ends."

choices.label: Read provision and service separately
choices.line: You ask the clerk to distinguish the family's maintenance from the duties expected in service. He repeats each part, leaving room for questions before assent.

choices.label: Name witnesses who can be found again
choices.line: You ask both sides to choose witnesses who live within reach. Their names are repeated aloud; the promise will have people attached to it after the officials depart.

beats.objective: Settle one immediate need before the household leaves.
beats.line: Outside, a dependant lifts a light grain sack and says nothing. The representative finally puts down the document. "If I return with fine words and this, they will know which one can be cooked."

choices.label: Ask for grain to be issued now
choices.line: You bring the keeper and representative together to count an immediate provision. The family takes away something useful while the larger arrangement is still being understood.

choices.label: Arrange a witnessed return to the household
choices.line: You ask the veteran to visit with the representative and hear the household's remaining claims. A time and meeting place are agreed in front of the local witnesses.

endings.text: The family leaves with the grant explained and an immediate provision counted. Service may follow; neither a signature nor a sack of grain makes the losses disappear. This household has reasons to test the new arrangement before trusting it.

The agreement travels out of the courtyard with named witnesses and a promised visit. You have made this household's claim harder to lose in a clerk's papers. Whether the promise survives will be learned at the next meeting.

The visitors have crossed the gate and heard the offer. A grant and a place in service begin a particular negotiation; they do not settle the loyalties of an entire clan. Your choices determine what this family can ask of the people who received them.

sequences.title: The Account Beyond the Curtain
sequences.location: A compressed public working court at Gujranwala
sequences.adaptation: Raj Kaur is Ranjit Singh's mother, distinct from the Nakai wife and paternal aunt of the same name. The source IDs support only the existing regency context. The Memorial's 1790 succession and the project's 1792 frame remain distinct. This hearing, its screen, all dialogue, fictional adult staff, courtyard, four grain bundles, orders and local outcomes are original dramatic reconstruction (D/C), not an authenticated event, account ledger or quotation. Privacy does not imply unauditable revenue, universal male exclusion or a female guard corps. A receipt and local arrival do not prove distant delivery. This optional telling changes no Home resources.
sequences.opening:
A runner waits for an answer before the road detail sets out. Four grain bundles stand beside the account desk. Raj Kaur will hear a report from behind the household screen; the records are in the working court. You are an adult clerk, carrying requests rather than ruling in her place.

This visit, dialogue and small supply account are original reconstruction. They are not a recorded Raj Kaur hearing. The visit's decisions remain within this telling.

beats.objective: Ask the attendant how to deliver your report.
beats.line: Attendant: She will hear you. Stand at the outer mark and speak for yourself. You need no permission to inspect the totals at the working desk. This admission does not open the private room.

choices.label: Request a direct hearing at the screen
choices.line: You are admitted to address Raj Kaur directly from the public hearing mark.

choices.label: Deliver a brief report from the public threshold
choices.line: The attendant admits your brief report. You will speak directly from the outer mark; no one needs to repeat your words.

beats.objective: Address Raj Kaur from the public hearing mark.
beats.line: Raj Kaur, behind the screen: The room may be private. The account must answer to someone. Which part of your request needs a witness?

choices.label: Ask for witnessed totals
choices.line: Raj Kaur: Let the clerk count in the working court. Write what is counted, and who saw it.

choices.label: Protect dependants’ names while opening the totals
choices.line: Raj Kaur: Keep their names off the public copy. The quantity and the receiver must still be inspectable.

beats.objective: Inspect the four bundles and the remount request.
beats.line: The account lists four grain bundles. The runner has also asked for a fresh horse. There is a request on paper, but no inspected animal here. The desk can be inspected without entering the private room.

choices.label: Count the four grain bundles
choices.line: You witness four bundles. The count is local and finite; no estate income or hidden treasury has been inferred.

choices.label: Check the remount note against the counted stock
choices.line: The note requests an inspection, not a promised horse. You also verify the same four bundles before carrying the request.

beats.objective: Request one bounded order for the waiting runner.
beats.line: Raj Kaur, behind the screen: We can issue two bundles and keep two here, or keep the grain and send a request to inspect a remount. One immediate need must wait. Which request will you carry?

choices.label: Request two bundles for the road detail
choices.line: Raj Kaur authorizes two of the four bundles. They will be handed to the runner when he acknowledges the order. Two remain at the desk.

choices.label: Keep the grain; request a remount inspection
choices.line: Raj Kaur retains all four bundles and authorizes an inspection request. No horse has been promised, bought or supplied.

beats.objective: Obtain the runner’s acknowledgement and accompany him.
beats.line: Runner: Read what I am receiving. I will not tell the riders a horse is coming if the paper promises only a look at one. I will walk with you to the gate.

choices.label: Read the order together
choices.line: The runner reads the limits back. He takes the written order and any issued bundles, then follows you toward the gate.

choices.label: Keep a sealed copy with a named receipt
choices.line: The runner acknowledges the limits and the sealed copy. He takes the order and any issued bundles, then follows you toward the gate.

beats.objective: Reach the departure gate with the actual runner.
beats.line: The runner has reached the courtyard gate beside you. You can request a household guard for his onward journey, or keep the post at home filled. A request is not a deployed guard.

choices.label: Request one household escort
choices.line: You record an escort request beside the order. A guard’s acceptance and onward departure remain unconfirmed.

choices.label: Keep the guard’s household post filled
choices.line: You make no escort request. The runner is here at the gate; his journey beyond it remains unconfirmed.

beats.objective: Return to the desk and record only the witnessed result.
beats.line: The account has a finite stock, one authorized order and a named recipient. You saw the runner reach this gate. You did not see a distant delivery, a remount arrive or a guard take the road.

choices.label: Record the order and local arrival
choices.line: You enter the authorization, the recipient and the local arrival together. The register leaves later delivery open.

choices.label: File the recipient’s receipt beside the count
choices.line: You file the named receipt beside the witnessed count and local arrival. The register leaves later delivery open.

endings.text: Two bundles have been issued and carried to the courtyard gate; two remain here. An escort is requested. No guard departure or distant delivery has yet been witnessed.
Two bundles have been issued and carried to the courtyard gate; two remain here. The household guard stays at the post. Delivery beyond this court remains unconfirmed.
All four grain bundles remain in the household. The runner has reached the gate with an inspection request and a request for an escort. Neither a fresh horse nor a guard departure is confirmed.
The grain and guard remain with the household. The runner carries a remount inspection request at the gate. An inquiry has been recorded; no horse has been acquired.
A private hearing has produced an inspectable account, a limited order and a named recipient. The record leaves later delivery open.
